problem: UICOMP-1: Badge had no way to set a DOM id, so consumers could not reference a badge (for example from aria-describedby) without reaching into the element by hand.
solution: Add optional `id?: string` to `BadgeProps` in src/components/badge/badge.ts. `updateBadge` (also used by `createBadge`) sets the id when a non-empty value is supplied and removes the attribute when it is omitted or empty, so full-props replacement leaves no stale id. Label and tone behavior and default markup are unchanged. No CSS, tokens, Storybook, or other components touched.
tests: npm run check (lint, format:check, typecheck, vitest 54 files / 656 tests, build, publint + consumer smoke, build-storybook) - all passed locally
New badge unit tests: no id by default; supplied id set on create without affecting label/tone; update changes id; update omitting id removes a previous id; update with empty string removes id
risks: Low. Additive optional prop, source compatible for existing callers. Design choice to flag: an empty-string id is treated as absent and removes the attribute (id="" is not a valid HTML id); reviewers may prefer otherwise.
review: Verify the removal path in updateBadge (removeAttribute('id') when id is omitted) and the test 'removes a previously set id when update omits it'. Confirm BadgeProps remains backward compatible and no files outside src/components/badge/ and .agent/ changed.
